title: dependability-partnership-compact-and-implementation-diary
summary: Working compact for a cross-team dependability pilot that focuses on operationalizing a minimal but pragmatic SLO surface across model-serving (serving-runtime), platform, and product routes. This file is a loose running diary + action list rather than a polished playbook. Use it to align stakeholders, capture tradeoffs, and store decisions during the 60-day pilot.
objectives: Define a single SLO schema for 3 canonical model-serving routes (inference-api, streaming-chat, embeddings) with clear measurement sources
Deliver an ops handoff pattern and lightweight runbook for outage and latency regressions (<= 2 pages per route)
Validate automated alerts and error-budget notifications across PagerDuty + Slack for two weeks of production traffic
Measure correlation between batching/caching changes and SLO signal to inform Optimize recommendations
milestones: Week 0: Kickoff with feature/product, serving-runtime, platform, and SRE — align objectives and signals
Week 1: Instrumentation spike — produce canonical metrics (p50/p95/p99 latency, availability, request-failure-rate, request-volume) and wire to observability namespace
Week 2: Draft SLO definitions and sanity-check with product on user-impact mapping
Week 3: Implement alert rules and simple incident playbook; run tabletop with oncall rotation
Week 4: Canary rollout of SLO-backed alerting for one region and 10% traffic
Week 5: Collect signals, tune noise thresholds, and update runbooks
Week 6–8: Full rollout for selected routes, measure error budget burn, and prepare retrospective + recommendations
roles_and_responsibilities: Marisol (SRE lead) — overall program owner, cadence, stakeholder coordination, retrospective
Lina (Serving Runtime) — provide route-level metrics, feasibility constraints for batching/caching impacts
Samir (Platform) — instrumentation hooks, namespace, and alert integrations
Omar (Product) — customer-impact mapping, SLO target signoff, and oncall liaison
Priya (Observability) — dashboard, tracing linkages, synthetic checks
Theo (Solutions Eng) — customer-facing messaging template and runbook review
timeline_summary: 60-day pilot, kicked off 2026-01-20. Fast feedback loops: weekly cross-functional syncs, bi-weekly tabletop, daily standup during canary week. Milestone gating: instrumentation -> SLO draft -> alerting -> canary -> rollout.
success_metrics: SLOs defined and stored in canonical repo (yaml) for 3 routes
Alerts fire with < 10% false positives during 2-week validation window
Error-budget burn correctly estimated and used in one automated fallback test
Mean time to detect (MTTD) reduced by 20% for injected latency incidents in canary window
Two runbooks finalized and verified via tabletop exercise
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Metric gaps for streaming-chat (partial traces). Mitigation: add synthetic end-to-end checks and client-side tagging as short-term patch
Risk: Noise from transient infra events causing alert fatigue. Mitigation: use short hold-off + rolling-window evaluation and tune thresholds during canary
Risk: Cross-team ownership ambiguity. Mitigation: embed SRE on product weekly sync; create ownership appendix with contact roster
Risk: Changes to batching invalidating historical baselines. Mitigation: label releases and run comparative A/B on a staging slice
communication_plan: Weekly summary email to stakeholders (SRE, runtime, platform, product, solutions) — template in linked artifacts
Daily slack #dependability-pilot during canary with rotated SRE monitor
Postmortem cadence: for any SLO breach > 1% error-budget burn in 24h, start a 72h investigation window and share RCA draft within 5 business days
Customer comms: Theo to draft 1-pager for customer-impact scenarios and escalation paths
open_questions: What is the final fidelity we accept for availability counting (successful HTTP 2xx vs semantic success for streaming tokens)?
How will reserved capacity (Dedicated) be represented in SLO targets vs hosted (shared) tiers?
Should error budgets be aggregated at product slice or route slice for initial pilot?
What is the rollback policy if canary causes downstream surge in platform queues?
decision_log: 2026-01-22: Agreed on p95/p99 latency + availability(>= 99.9%) as canonical SLOs for pilot routes — signed by Omar and Marisol
2026-01-28: Use Prometheus + trace linking as primary signal sources; synthetic checks supplement streaming metrics — decision by Observability owner
2026-02-05: Canary scope limited to us-east1 and 10% traffic for safety; automatic rollback if queue depth > threshold for 5m
